lessons.title: How sizing machines work and pre-start checks
lessons.html:
Why fruit is sized

Export and local markets buy fruit in fixed size or count classes. Every carton must contain fruit of one size range so that it packs neatly and meets the specification. The sizer separates the fruit into these classes and sends each class to the correct packing lane or bin.

Types of sizers

TypeHow it works
Mechanical (diverging roller or belt)The gap between rollers or belts widens; fruit drops through when the gap is bigger than its diameter
Weight sizerEach fruit is carried in a cup over a load cell and weighed; it is dropped at the outlet for its weight band
Electronic optical sizerCameras measure size, and often colour and external defects, and a computer assigns each fruit to an outlet

The operator's role

The operator sets the machine for the batch, monitors it, makes adjustments, keeps records and keeps it running safely. On electronic sizers this includes loading the correct program or recipe for the fruit kind, cultivar and market, and assigning outlets to lanes according to the packing plan.

Pre-start checks

  1. Confirm the batch: fruit kind, cultivar, producer, market and size classes required.
  2. Check that guards and covers are in place and emergency stops work.
  3. Check that the machine is clean and no tools or objects are left on it.
  4. Inspect belts, cups, rollers and chains for damage or wear.
  5. On electronic sizers, check camera lenses and lighting are clean, and calibrate load cells or cameras as the procedure requires, for example with test balls or reference weights.
  6. Confirm lane assignments with the packing supervisor.
  7. Warn people nearby before you start the machine.

Record the checks on the pre-start checklist. Do not run the machine if a safety device is faulty; report it and lock it out according to procedure.

lessons.title: Monitoring, adjusting and shutting down
lessons.html:
Monitoring during the run

A sizer is only as accurate as its settings. The operator must continually check that fruit arrives at the correct lane.

  • Sample checks: take fruit from each outlet at set intervals and measure with a sizing ring, caliper or check scale. Record the results.
  • Flow: watch the infeed. Too much fruit causes doubles (two fruit in one cup) and mis-sizing; too little wastes capacity. Coordinate with the tipping and pre-sort staff.
  • Lane balance: if one lane is overloaded and packers cannot keep up, fruit backs up and is damaged. Reassign outlets or adjust flow as agreed with the supervisor.
  • Handling damage: check drop heights and transfer points. Fruit should roll gently, not fall hard.
  • Machine condition: listen for unusual noises, check for slipping belts, jammed cups or fruit build-up.

Making adjustments

If sample checks show fruit in the wrong class, adjust the settings according to the manufacturer's instructions: roller gaps on mechanical sizers, weight bands or calibration on weight sizers, and size thresholds on optical sizers. After adjusting, recheck samples. Record every change and the reason.

Clearing jams safely

Never clear a jam while the machine is running. Press stop, apply lockout according to the site procedure, wait for all parts to stop moving, then clear the jam. Remove your lock and warn people before restarting.

Shutting down

  1. Run the line empty so no fruit remains on the sizer.
  2. Stop the machine in the correct sequence.
  3. Clean according to the cleaning schedule: remove fruit debris, wash cups and rollers with approved cleaners, and clean optical components with the specified materials.
  4. Report wear and faults for maintenance.
  5. Complete the shift record: batches run, sample results, adjustments, downtime and faults.

Key points

  • Sizers separate fruit into size or weight classes for packing.
  • Load the correct program and confirm lane assignments before starting.
  • Check guards, emergency stops and calibration before the run.
  • Take regular samples from each outlet and adjust when needed.
  • Always stop and lock out the machine before clearing jams or cleaning.

quiz.question: How does a weight sizer separate fruit?

options.text: By weighing each fruit over a load cell

quiz.question: What can happen when too much fruit is fed into the sizer?
Sample checks show fruit in the wrong class. What should the operator do?

options.text: Ignore it until the end of the shift
Tell packers to fix it by hand
Adjust settings per the manufacturer's instructions, recheck and record

quiz.question: What is the correct way to clear a jam?

options.text: Reach in quickly while it runs
Use a stick while it runs
Ask a co-worker to watch while you reach in
Stop, lock out, wait for parts to stop, then clear

quiz.question: Before starting an electronic sizer, which is a key setup step?

options.text: Load the correct program for fruit, cultivar and market

quiz.question: Every adjustment to the sizer should be recorded with the reason.
